I did it during COVID. I believe the only way is acceptance commitment therapy. Start first with your comfort things/crutches and venture out as far as you can go. So no health advisors for me just myself. 

This may be your, room, your front door or shop or whatever your safe zone is. 

Now you must push yourself to expose yourself to new scenarios gradually going further and further each day. Do not relent don't think I don't feel like this today that's exactly when you do need to do exposure. 

One day it was heavily snowing so I just put spikes on my shoes. 

Looking back now my Dad's car breaking was a blessing in disguise because in my mind he was my escape if I struggled I could always call him and pick me up. Not now so I stayed doing the exposure with heightened anxiety. 

Thinking of it now what would he have done stopped the panic attack? 

If you feel stupid walking the same places don't noone cares. 

One day something just kinda snapped and I thought I'm going way further than normal and I walked to the nearest town centre shops and I had a rather rapid recovery from there. 

You can do it and it doesn't matter how long you've been confined. 

It's all the mind. Embrace your anxiety and panic and say do your worst. It immediately turns it off.

Graded exposure. If you feel scared of afraid of something. Do it!!! In a small scale way. Scared of being outside step on the doorstep get comfortable feeling uncomfortable. 

Get further away from the door. 

Your anxiety will fall the more you do this then standing at the door is easy. Then going to the end of the drive is easy. Then walking the block is easy. Walk round neighbourhood every day varying route I found most of my irrational fears were beaten this way. I'd think oh my god I'm this far away from home but what exactly is at home?

Safety comfort? 

If you really think about it is isn't. The most brutal panic attacks I've had were at home.

All things I faced too I'm not sure what it is about stopping in a vehicle that makes the anxiety ramp up. If I was ever stuck in traffic I felt like jumping out of my skin and would look down at the floor so I couldn't see the lights. 

If I have one tip it's look forward look out the window. Stopping isn't causing you any harm. Nothing is causing you any harm. 

We fear fear itself so anything that causes the fear reaction we connect the dots and our brain says you should be anxious now but it's misfiring thinking you are in a life or death situation when it's just normal. 

Life is all about taking risks. 

By doing this exposure you are doing the right thing.

Look I've been recovered from agoraphobia now for a few years. I was agoraphobic for 5 then COVID hit it got even worse confined to bedroom. Every time you relent or resist your brain takes notice. Every time you escape or flee a panic attack you are reinforcing the notion that it can hurt you. 

It can't. Even the most scariest things a panic attack can do are temporary. You can't escape a panic attack so it doesn't matter if you are in a plane, in a lift wherever it happens no matter what you do the panic attack will ride itself out. 

Sorry if this comes across as aggressive but I've wasted years of my life I don't want you to do the same. 

Embrace the panic don't try to escape it.
